'''''Pitcairnia''''' is a [[genus]] of plants in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Bromeliaceae]], subfamily [[Pitcairnioideae]]. It was named after [[William Pitcairn]], Scottish physician and gardener (1711–1791).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://bsi.org/brom_info/genera.html |title=Bromeliad Society International – Genera Etymology |access-date=2007-02-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070203011214/http://www.bsi.org/brom_info/genera.html |archive-date=2007-02-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> ''Pitcairnia'' ranks as the second most species-rich genus in the family Bromeliaceae, after ''[[Tillandsia]]''. They are most abundant in Colombia, Peru and Brazil, but can also be found in areas from Cuba and Mexico south to Argentina. One species, ''[[Pitcairnia feliciana]]'', is found in tropical [[West Africa]], and is the only member of the family Bromeliaceae not native to the [[Americas]].<ref name=j>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=258274 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref>

Almost all ''Pitcairnias'' are [[Terrestrial plant|terrestrial]] or [[wiktionary:saxicolous|saxicolous]], and prefer moist areas. However, many are found growing [[epiphyte|epiphytically]] in trees.

==Taxonomy==
''Pitcairnia'' was established as a genus by [[Charles Louis L'Héritier de Brutelle]] in 1788.<ref name="IPNI_326845-2">{{citation |title=''Pitcairnia'' L'Hér. |work=[[International Plant Names Index|The International Plant Names Index]] |url=https://www.ipni.org/n/326845-2 |access-date=2022-11-02 }}</ref> In 1870, ''Pepinia'' was established as a genus by [[Adolphe-Théodore Brongniart]] in a publication by [[Édouard André]].<ref name="IPNI_4985-1">{{citation |title=''Pepinia'' Brongn. ex André |work=[[International Plant Names Index|The International Plant Names Index]] |url=https://www.ipni.org/n/4985-1 |access-date=2022-11-02 }}</ref> ''Pepinia'' was reduced to a subgenus of ''Pitcairnia'' in 1881 by [[John Gilbert Baker]],<ref name=EOB/> but elevated again to a genus in 1988, largely on the basis of the morphology of its seeds.<ref name=VaraGilm88>{{Citation |last1=Varadarajan |first1=G.S. |last2=Gilmartin |first2=A.J. |date=1988 |title=Taxonomic Realignments within the Subfamily Pitcairnioideae (Bromeliaceae) |journal=Systematic Botany |volume=13 |issue=2 |pages=294–299 |doi=10.2307/2419108 |jstor=2419108 |name-list-style=amp }}</ref> The use of morphological characters to differentiate ''Pepinia'' from ''Pitcairnia'' was rejected in 1999;<ref name=TaylRobiRobi99>{{Citation |last1=Taylor |first1=David C. |last2=Robinson |first2=Harold |last3=Robinson |first3=H.E. |date=1999 |title=A rejection of ''Pepinia'' (Bromeliaceae: Pitcairnioideae) and taxonomic revisions |journal=Harvard Papers in Botany |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=203–218 |jstor=41761301 |name-list-style=amp }}</ref> a view confirmed later by multiple molecular studies.<ref name=SchuKrapWagnWeis16>{{Citation |last1=Schütz |first1=Nicole |last2=Krapp |first2=Florian |last3=Wagner |first3=Natascha |last4=Weising |first4=Kurt |date=2016 |title=Phylogenetics of Pitcairnioideae s.s. (Bromeliaceae): evidence from nuclear and plastid DNA sequence data |journal=Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society |volume=181 |issue=3 |pages=323–342 |doi=10.1111/boj.12403 |name-list-style=amp |doi-access=free }}</ref>
